usage: "3afak" is the universal, everyday word for "please" in Morocco, used with everyone from close friends to shopkeepers. It is gender-neutral in practice and fits almost any casual or semi-formal situation. For more significant favors or when speaking to elders, Moroccans often switch to blessing-based requests like "llah ikhllik" (may God keep you).

variants.label: To a single person
variants.note: The standard, everyday form used when addressing either a man or a woman.

variants.label: To a group
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: More polite/respectful
variants.note: A respectful alternative often used with elders, officials, or strangers to show extra deference.

variants.label: Strong pleading
variants.english: please / may God have mercy on your parents
variants.note: Used when asking for a very big favor, asking for directions, or practically begging.

responses.english: here you go (if handing something over)

examples.english: Give me a kilo of tomatoes, please.
